purpose: External development-subject comparison without changing frozen FSM thresholds
interpretation: The front-view sample contains alternating bilateral motion, so the runner correctly avoids collapsing it to one selected arm.
Production detects seven repetitions on each arm in the front-view sample, while the stricter exploratory threshold misses some repetitions.
Production detects seven right-arm repetitions in the diagonal sample, while the stricter exploratory threshold detects none.
The frozen production threshold generalizes better than the exploratory full-contraction threshold on these two samples.
Near-zero front-view angle estimates indicate 2D projection degeneracy and must not be interpreted as anatomical elbow flexion.
No threshold will be changed until cycle-level human annotation and additional development subjects are available.
